findings.text: the Why states "a session's review sweep covers runs of other sessions in its project, so the row follows the sweeper and not the owner", but a session sweep is scoped to its own runs on both passes (recovery_review_acceptance.py:1590-1597; resumption.py:2767; station.py:460-461), so a live sweep cannot raise another session's failure: the row appears under a session that no longer owns the run only because the stored record outlived an ownership change, or because a caller sweeping without a session wrote it (resumption.py:2729-2735 allows a whole-fleet sweep)

findings.reason: the third deliverable adds a lifetime rule with no defect behind it, and a worker cannot write "returns when the error text changes" against a record that has no such field.
findings.text: "An acknowledgement of a sweep failure holds while the failure's error text is unchanged, whichever session's sweep reports it again" describes an error-text coupling the base does not have: acknowledgements are read per run id with an `until`/`until_condition` (obligations.py:1846-1917, `_partition_acknowledged` keys on `item["run_id"]`), and nothing in that record carries the failure's error text, so at the base an acknowledgement is neither held nor released by the text — the reported three acknowledgements in an hour are the symptom of the row being raised again, not of text churn
